summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel DPC watchdog profile cluster record. Repo docs list non-zero defaults for `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold` under `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Kernel`. Dedicated live KVM local-KD bundles now prove the mixed current-build global state plus the concrete reader, validator, and writer path: only `KeDpcWatchdogProfileOffsetMs` matches the repo-doc default while the other profile globals read as `0`, `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` only emits these fields when the globals are non-zero, `KiValidateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` backfills missing fields from the same globals and validates ranges, and `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` writes the globals from caller-supplied validated input. A later PDB-backed Ghidra symbol-xref pass narrowed the caller story further, a class-focused live KD pass then confirmed the exact runtime edge `NtSetSystemInformation+0x1bc9 -> KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, the admin-group gate, and a dispatch-chain inference that the writer arm is reached via numeric system-information arm `0xE4`, a dedicated live query-side KD pass now confirms the exact outer wrapper `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` while leaving the inner watchdog query arm unresolved, and a canonical init-semantics Ghidra follow-up then showed that current-build legacy/profile backfill only activates under sentinel/non-zero prerequisites. A later current-build INIT descriptor scan now also binds all four registry value-name strings to the same live globals, and a write-free KVM reboot observation confirmed the registry value states survive a real reboot unchanged. A target-specific WPR boot CSV filter found no exact runtime read for any of the four value names in the retained boot trace. The family is real, but the current build still does not support treating the repo-doc values as unconditional live defaults and runtime traces still have no exact registry read for the cluster.

validation_proof.exact_quote_or_path: Docs/system/system.md lists the `DpcWatchdogProfile*` values under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, and later KD/Ghidra follow-ups preserve the same profile family as a real current-build lane with explicit reader, validator, and writer proof.
validation_proof.notes: The current build has enough naming and structural proof for a documented draft, including current-build INIT descriptor rows for all four value names. What remains open is live default reconciliation, conditional-init semantics, and an exact runtime registry-read proof.

setting.name: Session Manager Kernel DPC Watchdog Profile Cluster
setting.area: Session Manager Kernel DPC Watchdog Profile
setting.casual_explanation: This cluster appears to control several DPC watchdog profiling thresholds inside the kernel. Current-build live state only agrees with the repo-doc default for the profile offset; the rest of the cluster currently reads as zero.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel and latency researchers may inspect these values when investigating DPC watchdog profiling thresholds, triage capture behavior, or internal watchdog diagnostics.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The family now has real current-build kernel-state evidence, conflicting repo-doc defaults for most values, a live-KD confirmed privileged runtime caller, and current-build INIT descriptor bindings for all four registry value names. It should stay a draft research cluster, not a tweak candidate.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs list four `Session Manager\\Kernel` DPC watchdog profile values with explicit defaults: `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes = 266240`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold = 110000`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset = 10000`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold = 18333`. A dedicated live KVM local-KD bundle later resolved the current-build `KeDpcWatchdogProfile*` symbol cluster and directly read the running globals. The result is mixed: `KeDpcWatchdogProfileOffsetMs = 10000`, but `KeDpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThresholdMs = 0`, `KeDpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThresholdMs = 0`, and `KeDpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes = 0`. The same pass also read the nearby control global `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0`, which is a useful contradiction against the older DpcWatchdogPeriod review lane that only proved the value is consumed when present. A second current-build KD disassembly pass then showed that `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is the concrete reader for the profile and control globals, and that it only sets result bits / copies fields when the globals are non-zero. The same disassembly bundle also showed that `KiValidateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` backfills missing fields from those globals and applies ordering/range checks, which gives the zero values direct default/fallback semantics in the current build rather than leaving them as uninterpreted noise. `KiUpdateProcessorDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is not the seeding caller; it only delegates to `KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits`. A later dedicated KD pass then showed that `KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits` itself is also downstream only: it forwards an already-built configuration block into `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` and does not read the watchdog globals directly. A subsequent KD pass narrowed the chain one more step: `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` copies fields from that prepared block into per-processor watchdog state and swaps the auxiliary profile buffer pointer when needed, but it still does not seed the globals. The dedicated writer pass then closed the writer question: `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` is the explicit current-build writer for the DPC watchdog globals. A later PDB-backed Ghidra symbol-xref pass tightened the caller picture again by showing that `NtSetSystemInformation` references `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, while `KiInitializeProcessor` references `KiCreateDpcLimitsProcessorConfiguration`. Existing deprecated DPC scheduler records then narrowed that interpretation further by already proving that adjacent DPC controls such as `AdjustDpcThreshold` and `DpcQueueDepth` are populated from the `NtSetSystemInformation` setter buffer and exported back through the query path. A later class-focused live KD pass then confirmed the exact current-build syscall edge at `NtSetSystemInformation+0x1bc9 -> KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, showed that the branch is gated by `SeAliasAdminsSid` membership via `RtlCheckTokenMembership`, and exposed the surrounding dispatch arithmetic. In that live dispatch window, the watchdog writer arm is reached after `ecx = ebx - 0xE0`, `sub ecx,1`, `sub ecx,1`, and `sub ecx,2` land on `je NtSetSystemInformation+0x1b95`, which implies `ebx == 0xE4` for the watchdog writer arm. That `0xE4` result is a live-disassembly inference about the numeric system-information arm, not a confirmed public class name. A later dedicated query-side KD pass then confirmed the exact outer wrapper edge `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` on the same current build, but the captured `ExpQuerySystemInformation` slice still did not isolate a symbolized `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` callsite. That narrows the query-side gap from `no live query lineage` to `inner ExpQuerySystemInformation watchdog arm unresolved`. A newly-canonical PDB-backed Ghidra init-semantics pass then added the missing current-build explanation for the mixed live profile state. `KiInitDpcThresholds` only clamps low non-zero control/profile inputs and deliberately lets zero-valued globals remain zero, while `KiInitializeLegacyWatchdogProfileThresholds` only derives profile thresholds and buffer size when legacy sentinel values `0xffffffff` are present and prerequisite control globals are non-zero. This means the current build has a coherent structural path where `KeDpcWatchdogProfileOffsetMs = 10000` can coexist with zero-valued profile thresholds and buffer size without implying a failed parser or a broken live read. That means the unresolved step is no longer a generic missing caller, privilege gate, or unexplained mixed state, but a narrower persisted-registry seeding caller, the exact inner `ExpQuerySystemInformation` query arm, plus the public/current-build class name, if any, for inferred numeric arm `0xE4` above a now-plausible runtime system-information lineage. A later host-side current-build INIT descriptor scan then found nearby `Session Manager\Kernel` rows for `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold`, each pointing to the same static RVAs as the live `KeDpcWatchdogProfile*` globals. A write-free KVM reboot observation then captured the registry cluster before and after a real host-driven reboot: `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset` stayed `REG_DWORD 10000`, the other three profile values stayed absent, the key stayed present, and the boot timestamp advanced from `2026-04-12T04:33:01.5000000Z` to `2026-04-12T14:17:36.5000000Z`. A target-specific filter over the retained `kernel-timing-wpr-boot-registry-20260412` WPR CSV then scanned `8248730751` bytes and found zero rendered hits for all four `DpcWatchdogProfile*` value names, even though that same trace family includes adjacent `Session Manager\Kernel` opens and value-level `QueryValue` rows. The unresolved step is no longer whether a current-build registry-seeding table exists, whether this registry state survives reboot, or whether the retained WPR CSV can preserve adjacent value names; it is which boot/init routine consumes those rows before the explicit writer/query path and how that interacts with the mixed `10000/0/0/0` live state.

evidence.title: Repo system docs list explicit DpcWatchdogProfile defaults
evidence.summary: Repo docs list `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes = 266240`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold = 110000`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset = 10000`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold = 18333` under `Session Manager\\Kernel`.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD bundle reads live DPC watchdog profile globals
evidence.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD bundle resolved the current-build `KeDpcWatchdogProfile*` symbol cluster and directly read `OffsetMs = 10000`, `SingleDpcThresholdMs = 0`, `CumulativeDpcThresholdMs = 0`, `BufferSizeBytes = 0`, plus control `KeDpcWatchdogPeriodMs = 0`.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly shows DPC watchdog reader and validator path
evidence.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` directly reads the profile and control watchdog globals and only sets output bits / copies values when the globals are non-zero, while `KiValidateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` backfills missing fields from the same globals and validates range constraints.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly excludes KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits as seeding caller
evidence.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KiApplyProcessorDpcLimits` forwards an input configuration block to `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` and does not directly read the watchdog profile globals.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly excludes KiSetProcessorDpcLimits as seeding caller
evidence.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KiSetProcessorDpcLimits` copies a prepared watchdog configuration block into per-processor state but does not directly read the watchdog profile globals.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD disassembly shows explicit DPC watchdog writer path
evidence.summary: A dedicated current-build KD disassembly pass showed that `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` validates caller input, writes the DPC watchdog globals under lock, applies the profile-buffer fallback, and then calls `KiCreateDpcLimitsProcessorConfiguration` to build the per-processor limits block.

evidence.title: PDB-backed KVM Ghidra caller pass ties DPC watchdog writer to runtime API and init consumer
evidence.summary: A PDB-backed current-build Ghidra symbol-xref pass showed that `NtSetSystemInformation` references `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, while both `KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration` and `KiInitializeProcessor` reference `KiCreateDpcLimitsProcessorConfiguration`.

evidence.title: Adjacent DPC scheduler records already prove NtSetSystemInformation setter/query lineage
evidence.summary: Existing deprecated DPC scheduler records already cite decompilation-backed proof that `NtSetSystemInformation` populates adjacent DPC globals like `KiAdjustDpcThreshold` and `KiMaximumDpcQueueDepth`, while the query path exports them back out. This narrows the watchdog writer interpretation to the same runtime system-information family.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD confirms exact NtSetSystemInformation callsite, admin gate, and inferred numeric arm
evidence.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD pass confirmed the direct edge `NtSetSystemInformation+0x1bc9 -> KeUpdateDpcWatchdogConfiguration`, showed that the branch is guarded by `SeAliasAdminsSid` membership via `RtlCheckTokenMembership`, and exposed the surrounding dispatch arithmetic that implies numeric arm `0xE4` for the watchdog writer path.

evidence.title: PDB-backed KVM Ghidra shows DPC watchdog init and legacy profile derivation semantics
evidence.summary: A PDB-backed current-build Ghidra xref pass showed that `KiInitDpcThresholds` and `KiInitializeLegacyWatchdogProfileThresholds` normalize or derive profile values only under specific non-zero / sentinel prerequisites, which explains why the current build can keep most profile globals at `0` even while `KeDpcWatchdogProfileOffsetMs` stays at `10000`.

evidence.title: Dedicated KVM local-KD confirms exact NtQuerySystemInformation wrapper into ExpQuerySystemInformation
evidence.summary: A dedicated live KVM local-KD pass confirmed `NtQuerySystemInformation+0x8c -> ExpQuerySystemInformation` on the running build and captured a larger `ExpQuerySystemInformation` dispatch slice, but that slice did not yet isolate a symbolized `KeQueryDpcWatchdogConfiguration` callsite.

evidence.title: Current-build INIT descriptors bind the DPC watchdog profile cluster to live KD globals
evidence.summary: A host-side current-build `ntoskrnl.exe` INIT descriptor scan found `Session Manager\Kernel` rows for `DpcWatchdogProfileBufferSizeBytes`, `DpcWatchdogProfileCumulativeDpcThreshold`, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset`, and `DpcWatchdogProfileSingleDpcThreshold` at file offsets `0xbed1e8`, `0xbed248`, `0xbed1b8`, and `0xbed218`. Those rows point to static RVAs `0xFC4048`, `0xFC4024`, `0xFC5FD4`, and `0xFC4028`, matching the live KD RVAs for the corresponding `nt!KeDpcWatchdogProfile*` globals; this closes the current-build static registry-seeding layer while leaving exact runtime registry trace evidence unresolved.

evidence.title: Host-driven KVM reboot observation preserves DPC watchdog profile registry state
evidence.summary: A write-free KVM reboot observation captured the `Session Manager\Kernel` DPC watchdog profile cluster before and after a host-driven reboot. The reboot was observed by boot-time change, the key remained present, `DpcWatchdogProfileOffset` remained `REG_DWORD 10000`, and the other three profile values remained absent, so the current registry state was preserved exactly across reboot.

evidence.title: Targeted WPR boot CSV filter finds no DPC watchdog profile exact runtime read
evidence.summary: A targeted filter over the retained `kernel-timing-wpr-boot-registry-20260412` boot CSV scanned the four `DpcWatchdogProfile*` value names and found zero hits. This target-specific no exact runtime read result keeps the runtime-read gap open while ruling out the retained boot CSV as evidence for these value names.

decision.why: The family is strong enough for a schema-backed draft because it has explicit repo-doc defaults, dedicated current-build live kernel-state proof, a concrete current-build reader/validator/writer path, a live-KD confirmed privileged `NtSetSystemInformation` writer callsite, a live-KD confirmed outer query wrapper `NtQuerySystemInformation -> ExpQuerySystemInformation`, current-build INIT descriptor bindings for all four registry value names, a write-free KVM reboot observation showing that the current registry state is preserved across a real reboot, and target-specific WPR negative evidence for the retained boot trace. It is not ready for promotion because the current build conflicts with the repo-doc defaults for most values, the exact inner query arm still has not been isolated, conditional initialization is still part of the explanation, and no exact runtime registry read has been captured. This remains active blocked work rather than an intentional hold because the family has a concrete current-build code path and the remaining gaps are specific proof gaps, not unsupported deployment risk.
